previously_reported_group.reported_status: plans discussed as prepared in the preceding year

remaining_group.original_target: similar plans planned to be developed by 2026

source.title: A working meeting was held on the development of multiple hazard risk management plans for Georgia’s river basins

source_claims: The Agency stated that plans prepared in the preceding year for Supsa, Natanebi, Kintrishi and Khobistskali were discussed.
The Agency stated that similar plans for the remaining seven basins were planned to be developed by 2026.
The notice names Enguri, Rioni and Chorokhi-Adjaristskali in western Georgia and Mtkvari, Alazani, Iori and Khrami-Ktsia in eastern Georgia.
not_established: The notice does not provide the four plan documents, approval decisions, publication URLs or implementation evidence.
A target for the remaining seven basins is not proof that the plans were completed by the target date.

source.title: A consultative meeting was held on the development of multi-hazard risk management plans for seven river basins

source_claims: The Agency stated that the validation process and results of multi-hazard risk assessments for seven river basins were presented to stakeholders.
The stated purpose was to refine identified risks through engagement with selected high-risk communities, confirm vulnerable areas and gather additional local information.
The notice does not name the seven basins in its text; the seven-basin list is separately named in the 2025 and 2026 Agency notices.
not_established: Presentation of risk-assessment validation results is not equivalent to formal approval of a multi-hazard risk-management plan.
The notice does not publish signed plans, map versions, model validation metrics or operational warning outcomes.

source.title: Organized by the Agency, consultative meetings were held regarding the preparation of multi-hazard risk management plans for the basins of seven rivers in Georgia

source_claims: The Agency reported a two-day consultation concerning preparation of multi-hazard risk-management plans for seven basins.
The notice names Alazani, Iori, Mtkvari, Khrami-Ktsia, Chorokhi-Acharistskali, Enguri and Rioni.
The notice describes institutional mandates, coordination and earlier 2026 analytical work on the disaster-risk-management framework.
not_established: The notice does not state that all seven plans were formally approved, adopted, published or operationalized.
No signed plan versions, approval decisions, map/model specifications or basin-specific exposure denominators are linked in the notice.

secondary_claim.claim_summary: The project page says plans were developed for seven basins, but the same sentence also contains the phrase 'for 4 river basins of Georgia'.
secondary_claim.interpretation: This is a secondary project-implementer statement with internally ambiguous basin-count wording; it is not primary proof of formal approval, publication or implementation.

fact: The 2025-10-06 Agency notice reports four plans discussed as prepared for Supsa, Natanebi, Kintrishi and Khobistskali and says the remaining seven were planned for development by 2026.
The 2026-04-02 Agency notice reports presentation of risk-assessment validation process/results for seven basins and community engagement to refine risks.
The 2026-11-25 Agency notice reports consultation on preparation of plans for the seven named basins.
inference: Risk assessment, community validation, plan drafting, consultation, formal approval, publication and implementation are distinct stages; the three Agency notices can describe successive or overlapping work without proving final plan approval.
The 2026-04-02 validation notice helps explain the workstream chronology but does not resolve whether final plan documents were approved by 2026-11-28.
unknowns: Whether each of the seven plans has a signed final version and an official approval decision.
Whether final plans and their maps/models are publicly available, and under what reuse terms.
Map scale, reference period, hazard scenarios, model validation, uncertainty, exposure denominators and implementation responsibilities for each basin.
Whether any plan has been translated into an operational warning, preparedness or anticipatory-action workflow.
